Au Sable River.source: Michigan DNR trout-stream classification / Michigan Fishing Guide
Au Sable River.notes: DNR classifies the Au Sable River in Crawford County as a Class I (self-sustaining wild trout) trout stream with ~69.1 miles of classified trout water. Verified species list from https://michiganfishing.guide/trout-streams/au-sable-river-crawford/ (data sourced from Michigan DNR Division of Fish and Wildlife). Wikipedia and DNR Trout Trails also confirm brown, brook and rainbow trout in the system.

Manistee River.source: Michigan DNR Status of the Fishery Resource Report 2020-283 / Michigan DNR inland trout regulations
Manistee River.notes: The Upper Manistee River flows through Crawford County (headwaters to Sharon, crossing Antrim/Otsego/Crawford/Kalkaska). DNR report 0345_2020_UpperManisteeRiver.pdf documents self-sustaining brook and brown trout populations and notes rainbow trout in tributaries; DNR trout regulations specifically regulate Brook, Brown and Rainbow Trout on the Manistee River (Crawford Co.) from Co. Rd. 612 to M-72 and from M-72 to CCC Bridge. Migratory salmon/steelhead are blocked by downstream dams and are not present in the Crawford County reach.
